data.name: Get ATS job position custom question
data.description: This endpoint returns one ATS job position custom question by numeric id. The data object includes nested custom_question_type and custom_answers. Requires permission to view that custom question.
data.evaluateGuide:
Returns one ATS job-position custom question by numeric identifier, including its type and answers. Use it to inspect a permitted custom question resource.

data.name: Internal DMAP Query Endpoint - POST https://internal.aws-prod.aws.epa.gov/api/query
data.description:
Internal (non-public) DMAP API endpoint referenced in the documentation. Use only if you have internal network access.
Documentation: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2023-12/dmap-api.pdf (references internal endpoint)
Quick Start:
- POST JSON body identical to the public query endpoint: {"query":"...","variables":{...}}
- Endpoint host: https://internal.aws-prod.aws.epa.gov
Parameters:
- query (required): GraphQL-like query text
- variables (optional): variables object
Common Errors & Fixes:
- Internal endpoint is likely restricted to internal network and/or IP allowlists; requests from the public internet will be blocked or return 403/404.
Edge Cases:
- This endpoint is listed as internal in the documentation; it may require VPN or internal AWS access and internal authentication not described in public documentation.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- None documented for internal endpoint in the provided PDF.
data.evaluateGuide:
Runs a GraphQL-style query against the EPA DMAP internal service using a JSON payload. It is intended for environments with internal network access.
Use for: Execute a DMAP query, pass query variables, retrieve portal data
Not supported: Public access, non-query mutations, external network access

data.name: Cancel Query by broker internal ID
data.description:
Cancel a running query by broker-assigned internal query ID. Requires the broker identifier and the broker's internal query id.
Documentation: https://docs.pinot.apache.org/release-1.4.0/for-users/user-guide-query/query-cancellation
Quick Start:
- Use the controller GET /queries endpoint to obtain the map of brokers -> internal query IDs.
- Issue a DELETE to /query/{brokerId}/{queryId} on the controller to request cancellation on the specified broker.
Parameters Explained:
- brokerId (required, path): Broker name/identifier as returned by GET /queries (e.g., Broker_192.168.0.105_8000).
- queryId (required, path): Broker-assigned internal ID for a running query (integer or string as returned by GET /queries).
- verbose (optional, query): true or false. When true controller may return details of per-server responses.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 404 Not Found: Specified broker or query id not found or the query already finished.
- 400 Bad Request: Malformed queryId or missing parameters.
- 403 Forbidden: Caller lacks permission to control queries (if controller is secured).
Edge Cases:
- This method is operationally heavier: you must identify the correct broker and internal id. It may return partial success information showing per-server response codes.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- No specific rate limits documented here; administrative APIs may be subject to operator-imposed throttles.
data.evaluateGuide:
Cancels a running Apache Pinot broker query using the broker identifier and internal query identifier in the path. Use it to stop active query execution.
Use for: Cancel a running query, stop broker execution, terminate query processing
Not supported: Starting queries, retrieving results, listing active queries

data.name: DMAP Query (Internal endpoint)
data.description:
Overview:
Internal DMAP endpoint intended for internal/privileged environments. Functionality is the same as production but the host and path differ.
Documentation: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2023-12/dmap-api.pdf
Quick Start:
- Create a POST request to {{baseUrlInternal}}/api/query
- Use a GraphQL body like: {"query":"...","variables":{}}
Parameters Explained:
- query (required, in request body): GraphQL-style query string.
- variables (optional, in request body): JSON object with GraphQL variables.
- Export formats and JSONP callback behave the same as production (/api/query/csv, /api/query/jsonp?callback=...).
Common Errors & Fixes:
- Same as production: 400 for bad queries, 408/504 for timeouts, 500 for internal errors. Internal endpoints may be subject to additional internal network or IAM restrictions.
Edge Cases:
- Access to this internal host is typically restricted to EPA internal networks; do not assume public availability.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Not documented publicly. Internal operational constraints may apply.
data.evaluateGuide:
Runs a GraphQL-style query against the EPA DMAP internal service with query text and optional variables in the JSON payload. It supports internal or privileged environments.
Use for: Execute a DMAP query, supply variables, retrieve grant data
Not supported: Public access, non-query mutations, external network access

data.name: Tracing Zipkin API - /api/v2/traces (debugging/query/zipkin/api/v2/traces)
data.description:
Proxy of Zipkin's /api/v2/traces endpoints with OAP debuggingTrace attached to results.
Documentation: https://skywalking.apache.org/docs/main/latest/en/debugging/query-tracing/
Quick Start:
- Use the same Zipkin query parameters as the standard Zipkin API when calling /debugging/query/zipkin/api/v2/traces.
Parameters Explained:
- All parameters are the same as Zipkin API /api/v2/traces (serviceName, spanName, minDuration, endTs/startTs, etc.). See Zipkin docs for full list.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400: Invalid Zipkin query parameters.
- 500: Backend processing error.
Edge Cases:
- Results will include an additional debuggingTrace field with OAP internal trace info.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Use Zipkin parameters as usual; large result sets may be truncated by backend or deployment limits.
data.evaluateGuide:
Queries distributed trace spans through Apache SkyWalking’s Zipkin-compatible debugging proxy. Use Zipkin query parameters to filter and inspect trace results.
Use for: Find traces, filter by service, filter by span, inspect durations
Not supported: Creating spans, updating traces, deleting trace data

data.name: Get internalDrops time series stats data of a single appliance filter by certain query parameters.

Data objects of each appliance is an array of data arrays, each data array contains the stats for a particular timestamp. Each number is data array corresponds to a name in COLUMN_DEF.  DATA object contains only values not keys.

data.name: Hex Tile / Query Internal Endpoint (enrich / extract)
data.description:
Query/internal endpoint used for Hex Tile enrichment and extract operations. The Query API supports enrichment and extraction of Hex Tile datasets.
Documentation: https://docs.foursquare.com/developer/docs/studio-data-sdk-reference
Quick Start:
- POST /internal/v1/query with JSON body describing the operation (type: enrich or other), input, and parameters. Include Authorization header and Content-Type: application/json.
Parameters Explained:
- type (body, required): process type, e.g., enrich.
- sourceId (body, required for enrich): UUID of Hex Tile dataset.
- sourceColumn / column / latColumn / lngColumn (body): columns used for enrichment/extraction.
- input (body, required): array describing target dataset(s) to operate on.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing token.
- 400 Bad Request: invalid or missing parameters.
Edge Cases:
- Extracting Hex Tiles uses the Query API; docs note contacting Foursquare if you wish to use Query API for extraction.
- Returns data in format controlled by Accept header (CSV, JSON, Arrow, etc.).
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Not specified on this page.
data.evaluateGuide:
Submits an internal Foursquare Studio Data API operation for Hex Tile enrichment or extraction. The JSON payload identifies the operation, dataset, and processing fields.
Use for: Enrich Hex Tile data, extract dataset data, process spatial columns
Not supported: Public place search, place editing, map visualization
